name: Most Terrifying Armor of the Air Dragon
notes: Dragon armor. Grants a Strength bonus of +2 (to a maximum of 8) and carries the Lightning Corona as an integral weapon (see weapons). Can hover, and for 5 further motes truly fly at up to 60 mph with limited manoeuvrability. The source prints the name as 'Most Terryfying' in the stat table and 'MOST TERRIFYING' in the heading. (Aspect Book: Air, p.81)

name: Buckler
notes: A small shield, between one and two feet across, used to actively parry incoming blows. It raises the difficulty to attack the character in hand-to-hand combat by 1 but does nothing to protect the character from missile fire. Exalted p.335.

name: Target Shield
notes: A large shield, able to effectively block missile fire; usually round or roundly triangular and often emblazoned with a device. Raises the difficulty of hitting the character in hand-to-hand combat or with missile fire by 1. Adds 1 to the mobility penalty of her armour, or inflicts a 1 point mobility penalty if she is using no other armour. Exalted p.335.

name: Tower Shield
notes: Twice as tall as a target shield and at least as wide. Increases the difficulty of hitting the character in hand-to-hand combat by 1 and of hitting him with ranged attacks by 2. Adds 2 to the mobility penalty of the character's armour, or inflicts a 2 point mobility penalty if he is using no other armour. Most tower shields have straps allowing the user to attach the shield to his body: in that configuration it protects as a target shield and leaves both hands free, but adds 1 to the fatigue value of the character's armour. Exalted p.335.

name: Myrmidon Carapace
notes: Articulated jade-and-alloy armour for 5 motes of attunement. The masked helmet integrates an Essence-scrying visor (night vision constant, no Essence infusions), an echo jewel and a mask-of-pure-breath filtration and voice system; the suit adds +1 to Strength for damage, lifting and feats. Weight class is not printed on the page — assigned Medium by comparison with the other Medium artifact armors (the Reinforced Buff Jacket Artifact sits at mobility penalty -1). (Mountain Folk p.283)

name: Pot Helm
notes: A rounded bowl that fits over the wearer's head, typically longer in the back than the front to protect the ears, usually with a nosepiece and a neck guard of chain or armoured leather, and often a spire cast into the crown to make a stunning blow atop it difficult to land. MECHANICALLY IDENTICAL to every other helm — helms are largely cosmetic, a substitute for a striking hair style. Optional gritty-game rule: a Storyteller may let opponents make called shots at a BARE-HEADED character's unarmoured pate by subtracting one success from the attack roll, an exception to the rule that called shots cannot cause extra damage. Exalted pp.334-335.

name: Masked Helm
notes: The standard helm for completing heavy armour: a thicker pot helm, usually without a spire, to which an armoured face plate can be affixed. The plate has holes for the eyes and mouth and is usually decorated with a ferocious beast — draconic images in the Realm, and in the Threshold the faces of dangerous beings such as Fair Folk warrior races, war spirits and predators like wolves and tigers. MECHANICALLY IDENTICAL to every other helm (see Pot Helm). Exalted pp.334-335.

name: Slotted Helmet
notes: One of the simplest and most durable helms: a cylinder rounded at one end and open at the other, the bottom typically fluted to let the wearer move her head, with a T-shaped slot in front to see, breathe and speak clearly. Usually cast as a single piece, which makes it very strong; often used to complete a suit of heavy armour where the craftsmanship is not up to forging a masked helm. MECHANICALLY IDENTICAL to every other helm (see Pot Helm). Exalted pp.334-335.
